title: Agent-skills QA eval cases (extended)
description: Schema for agent-skills/testing/<skill>/evals/evals.json. Extends the current judge-only shape (prompt/expected_output/expectations/files) with OPTIONAL functional-grading fields (seed, functional_check, trajectory_checks) so the QA harness can grade against a real MongoDB. All functional fields are optional and additive: existing knowledge-only cases validate unchanged. Fixtures referenced by `seed` live in the sibling `fixtures/` directory as deterministic <seed-name>.js scripts.

x-fixtureContract.description: The seed/fixture naming contract, declared here because it is shared across repos: agent-skills's validate-evals.mjs enforces it at authoring time and agent-skills-evals's solvers/seed_db.py resolves against it at run time. Both read these values rather than keeping their own copy, so the two cannot drift into a state where a case passes CI here and then fails to seed inside the harness.

^_.description: Author comment key (e.g. _note); ignored by the harness.

case.description: One test case. Single-turn cases use `prompt`; multi-turn cases use `workflow`.

id.description: Stable case id (unique within the skill; used to correlate results across runs).

prompt.description: The task given to the agent (single-turn). Required unless `workflow` is present.

workflow.description: Multi-turn task: ordered turns. Alternative to `prompt`.

expected_output.description: Narrative description of a correct answer. Lowest-priority judge target (used if no metadata assertions and no expectations).

expectations.description: Skill-level checkable criteria. Judge target when present and no per-case metadata assertions exist.

files.description: Relative paths (under the evals dir) of asset files inlined into the prompt.

seed.description: Names a DB fixture in the sibling fixtures/ dir (fixtures/<seed>.js), applied to the sandbox MongoDB before the agent runs. 'clean_slate' = empty DB (no fixture file). Required for any functional_check that reads real data.

trajectory_checks.description: Deterministic tool-use assertions on the agent's trajectory.

functional_check.description: Grades the agent's produced query/index against the seeded DB by RE-EXECUTING it (not trusting the agent's text). Discriminated by `type`.

oneOf.title: aggregation — re-run the agent's pipeline, compare returned docs

artifact.description: Path the agent writes its JSON pipeline array to, e.g. /workspace/pipeline.json.

expected.description: Expected result documents (subset of fields compared).

compare_fields.description: If set, compare only these keys of each doc.

oneOf.title: index — assert an index with the expected key exists

expected_key.description: An index key spec, OR a list of acceptable specs (any match passes — e.g. an ESR index and its reverse-scan inverse).

oneOf.title: explain — grade the query PLAN (robust to which optimal index was built)

require_ixscan.description: Winning plan must use an index (no COLLSCAN).

max_docs_examined_ratio.description: Fail if totalDocsExamined > nReturned * ratio (catches over-scan).

matcher.description: Selects tool calls in the trajectory. Combine fields (all must hold).

where.description: Param equalities the call's arguments must satisfy (path -> value).

success.description: Require the matched call's joined result to have succeeded (true) or failed (false). Implied by type=called_successfully.

trajectory_check.description: A mechanical tool-use assertion. `critical: true` gates the score; non-critical are recorded only.

type.description: called = the call was ATTEMPTED (passes even if it errored); called_successfully = the call was attempted AND returned without error. Prefer called_successfully for any gating check: counting attempts is what false-passed the AXP MCP investigation, where every mcp__mongodb__* call returned 'No such tool available' yet attempt-counting looked healthy.

oneOf.title: called / absent — a matching call must be present / absent
order — every `first` match precedes every `then` match
param — the matched call's arguments satisfy `match.where`
